title: Workstream registry
description: The workstream registry: which developer owns which repository paths. A workstream is an ownership declaration, not a lock — other developers' phases must keep their deliverables out of a claimed workstream's paths unless its owner approved the crossing. A claim is made by committing this file on the integration branch; a rejected push is the race signal. Cross-entry rules (unique ids, owners that are developer handles, non-overlapping paths, phases that stay out) are the workstreams check's, not this schema's.

workstreams.description: One entry per workstream, in the order the team chose. May be empty.

id.description: Permanent workstream id: unique in the registry and never reused for another workstream.

owner.description: Developer handle (an owners key in the systems registry that lists emails) when claimed; the empty string when open.

status.description: open: nobody owns the paths yet; claimed: owner holds them.

paths.description: Paths this workstream owns. A 'product:' prefix names a path in the product repository; an unprefixed path is in this repository.

items.description: One owned path, a file or a directory prefix.

interfaces.description: Documents describing what this workstream provides to the others.
